method.summary: Round 1 (2026-09-24): eight research lanes (Nexstar, TEGNA, Gray, Hearst, Sinclair/Scripps/Cox/Graham/Allen/independents, vendors and regional aggregators, southern states, historical data) each ran a researcher pass and a skeptic pass. Round 1 was rejected because none of its 233 leads had been checked first-hand and no Wayback capture counts existed. Round 2 (2026-09-25) ran four follow-up lanes, each with a skeptic pass: r2-priority re-checked the 28 highest-evidence leads and the drafted GitHub Actions probe; r2-cdx tried to measure Wayback captures for four storm windows; r2-gray-tegna chased Gray, TEGNA and Allen endpoints; r2-west-south covered Montana, Nevada, Wyoming and the missing Oklahoma, Louisiana and Mississippi stations. WebSearch stayed exhausted (200 of 200 calls) and WebFetch stayed blocked for every station, vendor, state and archive host, but WebFetch could load public objects on s3.amazonaws.com. That is how round 2 verified the first endpoints: 20 Gray Media per-station GSync exports (all explicitly empty) and a set of Allen Media count feeds. Provenance was otherwise checked through GitHub code search, raw file reads and git clones of public repos. This report merges all verified lane outputs, deduplicates stations found by several lanes, and keeps each station's verification status and how_found. Round-2 additions are marked in how_found and fetch_observation with 'Round 2'. Round 3 (2026-09-25) was requested because round 2 still had no Wayback counts and no populated list to test a parser against. It ran four lanes, each with a skeptic pass: r3-cdx retried the Wayback CDX counts for the Gray exports and the top 30 pages; r3-gray-s3 hunted for populated Gray exports and extended the S3 key pattern to about 70 more stations; r3-gray-probe independently probed 142 Gray call signs (101 keys exist, 41 return 404); r3-oo-state re-checked the NBC, CBS and FOX owned-station endpoints, WVEIS and Delaware. The tool state did not change: WebSearch exhausted, WebFetch blocked for every station, vendor, state and archive host, s3.amazonaws.com public objects reachable. Round 3 records are marked 'Round 3' in how_found and fetch_observation and carry round3 = 'new' or 'updated'. Round 4 (2026-09-25) was requested because round 3 still had no working source in the snowiest big metros (New York, Philadelphia, Boston, Baltimore-Washington, Pittsburgh, Chicago, Detroit, Minneapolis-St. Paul, Denver) and still no Wayback capture counts. It ran four lanes, each with a skeptic pass: r4-cdx prepared a fourth CDX plan (436 queries) and fetched the three populated Gray exports again; r4-northeast chased concrete endpoints for New York, Philadelphia, Boston, Baltimore-Washington, Pittsburgh and Buffalo; r4-midwest did the same for Chicago's Emergency Closing Center, Detroit, Minneapolis-St. Paul and Denver; r4-gray-terms looked for a readable copy of Gray Media's terms of use and robots.txt. The tool state did not change: WebSearch exhausted, WebFetch blocked for every station, vendor, state and archive host, s3.amazonaws.com public objects reachable. Round 4 records are marked 'Round 4' in how_found and fetch_observation and carry round4 = 'new' or 'updated'.
method.verified_definition: A source is 'verified' only when a web fetch tool running outside this container (WebFetch) loaded the page or endpoint at the reported URL and saw a closings list or an explicit empty state. Search results, GitHub copies and third-party code are provenance, not verification. Each verified record carries a verification_scope field that says exactly what was seen. Through round 4, every verified school-list endpoint is a Gray Media S3 GSync export: three returned real rows on 2026-09-25 (WSAZ, KWCH, WITN; fetched again about 02:20 UTC with the same rows) and the rest returned an explicit empty export. An empty export proves the endpoint exists and parses, not that the station still writes to it. Allen Media amb-feeds counters that loaded are recorded as verified count feeds; they hold a number, not schools, and never count as school-list sources. 'unverified' means the URL has a documented source but no live check succeeded. 'refuted' means the evidence shows the URL is not a usable closings source (dead host, constructed URL, one-off article). role 'url_unknown' marks a station known to belong to a platform family whose current closings URL was never observed; it is kept but not counted as a lead. Every endpoint gets a direct check once the container can reach it.
counting_rules: A station counts once, however many lanes reported it. Evidence from each lane is merged into its how_found text.

unverified_stations per state counts live leads (stations, aggregators, state systems and vendor feeds with a documented current URL) whose states list includes that state. Multi-state assignments often come from market geography, not from inspecting a list.

Pointer records (a station that only links to another source), count-only feeds, URL patterns without a station, historical-only records and refuted records are kept in the stations array but not counted as leads.

Reach estimates count schools in the Snowlight directory (pipeline/out/internal/directory/schools.parquet, NCES 2024-25 public and 2023-24 private, continental US) within 60 miles of each lead's market city (Census 2025 Gazetteer place centroid). Statewide systems count every school in their state. This is a planning proxy for how many schools an adapter could plausibly cover, not a measure of what any list contains.

verified_stations per state counts stations whose school-list endpoint is verified (rounds 2 to 4: all are Gray S3 exports). A multi-state station counts in every state it lists; secondary states for the new Gray stations come from market geography (background knowledge).

verified_count_feeds per state counts stations whose Allen Media amb-feeds counter returned an explicit numeric count to a web fetch tool (blank strings and the 999 sentinel do not count). They are not school-list sources and are not in verified_stations.
Stations with role 'url_unknown' (a platform member with no observed closings URL) are listed per state under stations_without_url and are not leads.

Round 3 moved five stations (KBJR, KTIV, WEEK, WBNG, WVVA) from Newsroom Solutions and one (WJRT) from Allen Media to Gray GSync because a grayfilestore export exists under their call sign. That shows where their closings data lives now, not who owns them.

A Gray S3 key that returned HTTP 404 is recorded under refuted_endpoints on the station record when one exists, and in gray_s3_key_probes otherwise. It refutes that URL only, not the station as a source.

Round 4 changed two terms statuses. Scripps is now a known blocker: a third-party snapshot of the WXYZ Terms of Use bans robots, spiders and scraping without written permission, as the Nexstar and Hearst copies do. Gray is now a likely blocker: a third party's close paraphrase of the Gray Local Media terms bars non-browser software agents and commercial reproduction without written permission. It is a paraphrase, not the text, so it is 'likely', not 'known'.

Because every verified endpoint is now Gray, the recommended build order leaves out only the known blockers (Nexstar, Hearst, Scripps). Likely blockers (Gray, TEGNA) stay in the engineering order, but their adapters do not poll in production or publish rows until someone reads the actual terms from the runner and, where needed, gets written permission.
Round 4 added two platform families (Graham Media's Arc site for WDIV, and Hubbard's School Alert pages) and moved WNYT from the one-off group to Hubbard.

The three populated Gray exports (WSAZ, WITN, KWCH) were fetched again about 02:20 UTC on 2026-09-25 and returned the same rows, and the WKTV and KWWL counters read an explicit 0 again. Every station, vendor, state and archive host the four lanes tried (about 60) was blocked.

Big metros. Two lanes chased the ten snowiest big metros. They added 17 records: WDIV, WXYZ and a CBS Detroit record; KSTP, WDIO and FOX 9 (Minneapolis-St. Paul and Duluth); KMGH and a CBS Colorado record (Denver); FOX 32 and ABC7 Chicago; ABC7 New York, WCBS, News 12 Long Island and Spectrum News 1 Capital Region; 6abc; WFXT Boston 25 and WHDH. Five of them have no current closings URL. None could be verified. The most promising new lead is WDIV (Detroit): its page embeds the closings list as JSON, so a plain fetch and a Wayback page capture should both see rows. The big-metros table below lists what each metro has.

Terms. Gray moved from 'unread' to 'likely blocker': a third party's close paraphrase of the Gray Local Media terms bars non-browser software agents and commercial reproduction without written permission. Scripps moved to 'known blocker': a snapshot of its terms bans robots and scraping without written permission. Every verified endpoint is Gray's, so every verified endpoint now sits behind a likely terms blocker. The recommended build order now leaves out only the known blockers (Nexstar, Hearst, Scripps) and marks Gray and TEGNA as build-but-hold: build and test the adapter, but do not poll in production or publish rows until the verbatim terms are read and permission is granted where needed.

Corrections. The WTAE populated fragment and its cited file path were not found; the KDKA path cited in earlier rounds does not exist (the empty-list fragment is in another file); the NBC10 '38 School Closings' header, the WCVB and WBAL nav links and the KWWL counter call could not be found by the fetch tool (possibly truncated reads), so they are now unconfirmed. KWCH's row does not show that expired rows are served: at fetch time it had not yet expired in Central time. For the path-style S3 URLs, the governing robots.txt is https://s3.amazonaws.com/robots.txt, which returns 403 (no restrictions). The Emergency Closing Center's operator is unconfirmed. NBC 5 Chicago's site config names its own closings page as well as linking to ECC.
Two new platform families: Graham Media's Arc site (WDIV) and Hubbard's School Alert pages (KSTP, WDIO, and WNYT moved from the one-off group).

Wayback: still no capture count after four rounds. A fourth CDX plan (436 queries, covering all 123 Gray keys) is drafted and its test passes on fabricated fixtures. It can only run as a GitHub Actions workflow pushed to the repo, pushing it starts the run, and the user has not approved the push. The one user message relayed during this round ('I'm on mobile it's not there') is not an approval.
round_3_changes: First real rows. On 2026-09-25 about 01:37 UTC the Gray exports for WSAZ (3 Gallia County OH schools, 'Closed Friday'), WITN (3 Pamlico County NC rows, two-hour delays) and KWCH (1 Grant County KS row, 'Alert Thursday', mud routes) held records, and a second lane saw the same values about 01:50 UTC. The Gray item schema (19 keys) is now known, and the seven rows are embedded in sources.json as parser fixtures. None is a winter-weather event, one is not a closure, and one is a community college.

Gray key probe. Two lanes extended the S3 key pattern: 103 more keys exist, for 123 in all, and all but those three were explicitly empty. That added 70 station records and moved 33 existing records to verified, including WALA (Mobile) and WSMV (Nashville, which had only a 2011 URL). KBJR, KTIV, WEEK, WBNG, WVVA (from Newsroom Solutions) and WJRT (from Allen Media) moved to the Gray platform because their exports exist. 41 call signs have no grayfilestore bucket, including every Montana station tried, most of Idaho and the ex-Quincy and Allen stations. KY3 and WGCL (Atlanta News First) buckets use brand and former call-sign names.

Correction: round 2 said the Gray export changed shape (record[] to locations[]). It did not. Populated files carry record[] for items and locations[] for state names; the empty form simply omits record. A 2017-2024 web page and a February 2025 Home Assistant sensor read the same record[] fields, so Wayback captures back to at least 2020 should parse with one parser.

NBC, CBS, FOX, WVEIS and Delaware (r3-oo-state): every host was blocked again. Provenance was re-read for every URL and all of it holds, so nothing is refuted. The CBS Chicago page that the lane added is already in this report as an Emergency Closing Center pointer.

platforms.name: Nexstar WordPress closings page ('nxs' platform, from Lakana), incl. PSG iframe variant (KSN)
platforms.operator: Nexstar Media Group (also sites it runs for Mission Broadcasting and White Knight)
platforms.endpoint_type: HTML page; WordPress REST {origin}/wp-json/wp/v2/pages?slug={slug} (content.rendered); PSG iframe on media.psg.nexstardigital.net
platforms.polling_notes: Expect HTML pages to return 403 to bots (Glance README for fourstateshomepage.com; KTLA notes in rlorenzo/chino-valley-today). The wp-json route is what Glance uses (TTL 300 s). Slugs drift: /weather/closings/, /weather/closings-delays/, /weather/closings-and-delays/, /weather/closings-2/, /closings/. On some sites /weather/closings/ was a category archive (conchovalleyhomepage.com 2020), where pages?slug=closings returns nothing. Empty state: 'Most recent closings and delays are listed here when there are active closures.' Whether rows are server-rendered or inside an iframe is unknown (WRIC capture has 'no iframe support!').
platforms.terms: Known blocker, now from two independent copies. tosdr/tosdr-snapshots 'Nexstar media group/Terms of Service.html' (Terms of Use effective April 19, 2023; snapshot commit 2024-07-31) bans using 'any robot, spider, spyware, or any other device, method, or processes on the Properties, for any purpose' and says users may not 'Scrape, data-mine or data-crawl the Properties or engage in any data gathering or data extraction practices for any purpose'. A third-party read on 2026-08-19 (rlorenzo/chino-valley-today) quotes the same clauses and a restriction on AI use. The terms cover Nexstar 'Affiliates' ('any entity that we control, are controlled by, ...'), which after the 2026 acquisition may already reach TEGNA sites. Not read first-hand on nexstar.tv. Get written permission before polling.

platforms.name: Emergency Closing Center (Chicago aggregator)
platforms.operator: Unconfirmed. The only evidence is glance's label 'CBS Chicago / WGN Radio widget on CBS'; the subdomain name wgnr-closings fits a WGN Radio link, but no source names the operator
platforms.endpoint_type: React SPA at wgnr-closings.emergencyclosingcenter.com (JS-only; no public JSON/XML found); legacy static complete.html
platforms.polling_notes: Capture the XHR behind the SPA from a real browser before building. CBS 2 embeds it and NBC 5 links to it, so one adapter covers Chicago TV. The drafted CDX plan uses a host-wide prefix on www.emergencyclosingcenter.com, which would count unrelated pages and misses the wgnr-closings subdomain; query wgnr-closings.emergencyclosingcenter.com/ and www.emergencyclosingcenter.com/complete.html instead. Round 4: no data request behind the app has been seen in any public source; the next step is a one-time browser devtools capture. NBC 5's saved site config names its own /weather/school-closings/ page while its nav links to ECC, so NBC 5 may run both.

platforms.name: TEGNA /closings module
platforms.operator: TEGNA (Nexstar-owned since 2026, run separately under court order)
platforms.endpoint_type: HTML page https://www.{domain}/closings; no public data endpoint (glance: 'listing is server-rendered on the page'; guessed JSON paths 404)
platforms.polling_notes: Classes closings__list / closings__item / closings__title / closings__body; empty state 'No delays or closings.' Server rendering of a populated list is inferred from empty pages only. Page titles differ by station, so one parser across stations is unproven. /feeds/syndication/rss/weather/closings is news articles, not the list. Intake runs through /closings-admin paths and schoolclosings.org logins; never poll those. Round 2: molin6/ClosureAlerts (2024) polled https://www.5newsonline.com/closings every 5 minutes with plain requests.get and parsed li.closings__item > span.closings__title + span.closings__body; matt-kruse/qcweatherwatch.com (2020) scraped WQAD with an empty-state class closings__no-results, while glance (2026) reports closings__error, so a parser should accept both. KSDK pages carry a header alert (header__alert_type_closings) linking /closings. Round 4: 2020 KARE 11 and 9NEWS homepages carry a header flag a.header__alert_type_closings with a header__alert_visible_false class, which could gate polling. glance's populated row classes come from CSS, not from a populated page.
platforms.terms: Likely blocker. Round 2 read the tegna.com corporate Terms of Service in tosdr/tosdr-snapshots ('Last Updated: January 26, 2019'; snapshot commit 2024-09-11). It has no robot or spider clause, but says 'Accessing the Site, in any manner, whether automated or otherwise, constitutes use of the Site', 'The Site is provided solely for your personal noncommercial use', bars modifying, copying, reproducing, republishing or distributing 'any material from the Site', and bars incorporating 'into another website or other service any of our material' without prior written permission. That bears directly on republishing closings on a map. The station-site terms (wusa9.com and others, reportedly dated 2025-06-26) are still unread, and Nexstar's 'Affiliates' clause may now apply. robots.txt: 2019 copies for wfaa.com and 9news.com (scrapy/protego tests, commit ceab4fc) do not disallow /closings; current files unread. Include TEGNA in the Nexstar permission request.

platforms.name: Gray Media GSync closings (Arc XP pages; Arc gsync-closings endpoint; per-station S3 export)
platforms.operator: Gray Media (formerly Gray Television, incl. Raycom, Meredith local and Quincy stations), inferred from the grayfilestore bucket prefix and the body field source 'GSync'. glance says Allen Media's WTHI also runs Gray GSync, so an export does not prove Gray ownership (WTHI, WLFI, WTVA and WJRT also have Allen counters)
platforms.endpoint_type: Verified: per-station S3 JSON export https://s3.amazonaws.com/grayfilestore-{call}/closingsData/closings_{CALL}.json (also served at grayfilestore-{call}.s3.amazonaws.com). Populated: [{record:[items], locations:[state names], num_closings, export_type 'L1', source 'GSync', run_date ''}]; empty: the same without record. Also: Arc Fusion JSON {origin}/pf/api/v3/content/fetch/gsync-closings (list form never seen; only a count, totalResults, in saved pages) and a NewsTicker XML fallback via newsticker_url.
platforms.polling_notes: Round 3 saw the first populated files: WSAZ (3 Ohio schools, 'Closed Friday'), WITN (3 rows, two-hour delays) and KWCH (1 'Alert' row, 'Running Mud Routes') on 2026-09-25 about 01:37 UTC, each matched by a second lane about 01:50 UTC. The other 120 verified keys returned the identical explicit empty export. Items have 19 keys; see the station endpoint_format. Parser rules from the rows seen: items live in 'record', which is absent when num_closings is 0; locations[] holds title-case state names, not items; forced_county_name holds the state in capitals and county_name1 the county; forced_category_name is 'Schools' at two stations and 'OH' at WSAZ, so do not filter on it; forced_status_name is free text with the weekday built in, and 'Alert' is not a closure; comments_line1 is null or a string; rows are per building (River Valley High and Middle School) and include non-K-12 organizations (Pamlico Community College); expiration has no time zone (KWCH's 23:30 row was still served at 20:37 CDT, which fits station-local time); updated is a date only, so latency cannot be measured from the file; run_date is always empty. rec_ids run 398986 (KWCH), 398994-398996 (WSAZ) and 398997-398999 (WITN), which suggests one shared sequence, so a school posted to two stations probably gets two rec_ids: deduplicate on normalized organization name plus zipcode, then match to NCES. WebFetch shows no Last-Modified, ETag or Cache-Control headers, so the runner's first raw poll should record them and save raw bytes. Controls: a missing key in an existing bucket returns 403, a missing bucket 404, bucket roots 403. The only public consumers read data[0].record (matt-kruse/qcweatherwatch.com, 2017-2024; pacorain/toad Home Assistant sensor, February 2025). Arc route: glance requests the bare gsync-closings path; saved Arc pages hold a count with a 120 s cache TTL. Round 4: the WSAZ, WITN and KWCH exports were fetched again about 02:20 UTC on 2026-09-25 and returned the same rows. The DuckDuckGo tracker-radar crawl of 2026-09-16 shows wave3.com and wdrb.com loading gsync-closings from www.wdrbwave.com, a different host from the page's own origin, so the Arc fallback cannot assume origin plus path for every station.
platforms.terms: Likely blocker (round 4). The only readable copy is a third party's close paraphrase, not Gray's text: wbuscombe/mymts docs/findings/25-local-station-sourcing-wcia-week-wand.md (dated 2026-09-25 UTC) says 'The Gray Local Media Terms of Service permit viewing, sharing, linking or caching for personal, non-commercial use with notices intact; bar reproducing, distributing, transmitting, linking or caching for commercial purposes without written permission; bar framing; and bar using any engine, software, tool or agent to navigate or search the Services other than Gray's own search and generally available web browsers, naming artificial intelligence and intelligent agents among them.' It reports WAND's terms as the same text as WEEK's. It gives no section numbers or effective date. Whether a scheduled fetch of the S3 exports on s3.amazonaws.com counts as navigating 'the Services' is unknown, but republishing rows on a map would fall under the commercial reproduction clause if Snowlight is commercial. Gray's own terms pages (e.g. kcrg.com, atlantanewsfirst.com and wandtv.com /terms-of-service/) and the Gray AI-policy PDFs (gray.tv and graymedia.com) are all EGRESS_BLOCKED. robots.txt: no Gray station file has been read; a 2026 probe of hawaiinewsnow.com (shoalresearch) records a 1,225-byte robots.txt that names GPTBot and ChatGPT-User, rule text not stored; TowCenter's November 2024 table marks all 14 Gray sites only in the PerplexityBot column, with the mark undefined. Gray article pages carry meta robots 'noarchive' (KCRG 2026, WBRC 2021). The S3 objects carry no license, and their robots.txt (host s3.amazonaws.com) returns 403, which RFC 9309 treats as no restrictions. Read the verbatim terms from the runner, then ask Gray for written permission before polling in production or republishing rows.

gray_s3_key_probes.pattern_source: matt-kruse/qcweatherwatch.com index.html line 176 (the KWQC key). Every other key was built from it and then fetched.
gray_s3_key_probes.controls: A missing key inside an existing bucket returns 403 (grayfilestore-kwqc/.../closings_NOPE.json, closings_XXXX.json; grayfilestore-wkyt/.../closings_WAVE.json; grayfilestore-kolo/.../closings_ZZZZ.json). A made-up bucket returns 404 (grayfilestore-zzzz, grayfilestore-zzzq). Bucket roots return 403, so nothing can be listed. Robots: for crawler purposes the robots.txt that governs the path-style URLs is https://s3.amazonaws.com/robots.txt (round 4 correction); S3 reads that path as a bucket named 'robots.txt' and returns HTTP 403. The virtual-host form grayfilestore-kwch.s3.amazonaws.com/robots.txt also returns 403. Under RFC 9309 a 4xx robots response means the file is unavailable and crawling is unrestricted, so robots exclusion is unlikely to explain any missing Wayback captures.
gray_s3_key_probes.no_bucket_404_note: 39 of these were found in round 3 (the probe lane's count of 41 includes earlier probes); KADN and KOCO come from round 2, which had also probed KWTV. Alternate names worked for two stations: KY3 (not KYTV) and WGCL (not WANF). Not tried: brand or former call sign names for WREX, KGIN, KDLT, KSCW, KSVT and the rest.

gaps.description: The snowiest big metros still have no verified school-list source after round 4: New York, Philadelphia, Boston, Baltimore-Washington, Pittsburgh, Buffalo, Chicago, Detroit, Minneapolis-St. Paul and Denver. Round 4 aimed two lanes at them. It added 17 records (WDIV, WXYZ, KMGH, KSTP, WDIO, FOX 9, WABC, 6abc, WFXT, WHDH, News 12 Long Island, Spectrum Capital Region, and five stations with no current URL) and re-checked the provenance of every existing lead, but every station host was blocked, so none could be verified. The best candidates are those with evidence of a working list and no known terms blocker: WDIV (list embedded as JSON in the page), the Emergency Closing Center (needs its data request captured), WPXI and WUSA9 (populated Google fragments in March 2026), KARE 11, KSTP and the NBC and FOX owned stations.
